1269ee826b6f1d4e.title: 2027 Summer Associate - Restructuring & Special Situations Group
1269ee826b6f1d4e.description:
PJT Partners is a global advisory-focused investment bank. Our team of senior professionals delivers a wide array of strategic advisory, shareholder advisory, restructuring and special situations and private fund advisory and placement services to corporations, financial sponsors, institutional investors and governments around the world. We offer a unique portfolio of advisory services designed to help our clients achieve their strategic objectives. We also provide, through PJT Park Hill, private fund advisory and fundraising services for alternative investment managers, including private equity funds, real estate funds and hedge funds.

 From the beginning, PJT Partners has firmly believed that having the best people is key to building an enduring franchise. Our perspective was, and remains, that a great team brings in both top tier clients and appeals to a wide-range of diverse, talented colleagues. Fostering an inclusive culture, which welcomes differing perspectives and beliefs, enables us to provide the best advice and insights to our clients.

 To learn more about PJT Partners, please visit our website at   www.pjtpartners.com . 

 Program Description: 
 The Restructuring and Special Situations Group (“RSSG”) advises both large and middle market companies, financial sponsors and creditor groups in financially distressed situations, both in Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings as well as in out-of-court restructuring, capital raising and strategic advisory transactions. Founded in 1991, the RSSG team consistently maintains an industry-leading market share, having advised on many of the largest and most high-profile reorganizations and liability management transactions that have occurred in the last decade.

 Across restructuring and liability management transactions, the team provides a wide range of strategic advisory services, including analysis and advice on recapitalizations, reorganizations, exchange offers, distressed mergers and acquisitions, raising debt and equity capital, and providing expert witness testimony on a range of topics including corporate valuations.
 Upon completion of training, Summer Associates in the Restructuring & Special Situations Group will have the opportunity to develop a broad corporate finance skillset. Financial restructuring transactions are inherently complex and involve multi-party negotiations with several key stakeholders including, among others, a board of directors, management, secured and unsecured lenders, equity holders, and, at times, the bankruptcy court. Summer Associates are integral to all aspects of a deal and are involved with the development, structuring, and financing of transactions, and regularly attend both client and internal meetings, negotiations, and due diligence sessions. Summer Associates receive exposure to and training on the full spectrum of complex issues that arise in restructurings, including valuation analysis, capital raising, mergers and acquisitions, asset sales, credit negotiations, exchange offers and Chapter 11 reorganizations, while coordinating closely with their deal teams and often working directly with senior level bankers. 

 Responsibilities: 
 Summer Associates have responsibility for guiding transactions on a day-to-day basis. These responsibilities include:
 Performing due diligence with the client;
 Developing detailed business plans;
 Building comprehensive financial models to be used as part of restructuring transactions, capital raises, and/or corporate valuations;
 Analyzing credit and other legal governing documents;
 Evaluating financial returns to current and potential investors;
 Attending key client negotiating and strategy sessions;
 Assisting in the preparation of a plan of reorganization and disclosure statement materials for Chapter 11 cases; and
 Managing and developing all key client deliverables.

 Qualifications: 
 PJT Partners seeks to hire individuals who are highly motivated, intelligent and have excellent academic, leadership and extracurricular records. In addition, qualified candidates will possess the following:
 Strong interest in restructuring and distressed finance (prior experience in restructuring is not required)
 Outstanding qualitative, technical, and analytical skills
 Professional and confident communication skills to interface with senior management at clients and internal deal teams
 Strong work ethic with the ability to thrive in a collaborative and team-oriented culture
 Robust organizational and time management skills
 Robust knowledge of accounting and corporate finance

 Requirements: 
 To be considered for the 2027 Summer Associate Program, applicants must meet the following criteria:
 Currently enrolled in an MBA program*
 Anticipated graduation date: December 2027 – Spring 2028
 Resume must include expected graduation month/year
 Completion of “Suited” Assessment. Please see below for more details.

 * Undergraduates and experienced hires should refer to the Campus Analyst or Experienced Hire opportunities listed on our career site.

 Suited Requirement: 
 Complete the PJT Partners “Suited” Assessment. Please CLICK HERE to create an account. Suited is an A.I. powered assessment driven screening tool that uses assessments to holistically and objectively measure traits and characteristics that can be better predictors of success at PJT. Please ensure you use the same email address used for your PJT application when registering on Suited. Please complete each question through the end of the survey. A “Profile Complete” badge will appear once complete - there is no final “Submit” button.

 Expected Annualized Base Salary of $225,000
Time type: Full time

Our Capital Markets Advisory Group provides equity and debt advisory services to a wide variety of clients, from multinational, public corporations to privately held companies either sponsor-backed or founder-owned. The Capital Markets Advisory team works in partnership with PJT Partners’ Strategic Advisory, Park Hill, Restructuring and Camberview teams.

 Conducting financial and other business-related research
 Coordinating and helping manage complex and often time-sensitive capital raise processes
 Facilitating due diligence and discussions with clients, legal counsel, investors, and advisors
 Active involvement in live client facing situations
 Assistance in the execution of transactions
 Assistance in deal structuring (covenants, key terms, etc.) and term sheet negotiations
 Ongoing investor relationship development and management
 Constructing and managing internal deal and investor-related databases

b5e5d929c6da04e5.description:
Company 
Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago 

Are you a curious, quantitatively skilled recent graduate who wants to understand how economic research informs real-world policy? Join the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago’s Research Assistant Program and work alongside economists and researchers on important questions facing the economy, financial markets, businesses, and households.

As a Research Assistant, you will gain hands-on experience across the research process, including managing data, conducting econometric analysis, answering economic questions, and communicating results through compelling charts, written analysis, and presentations. You will contribute to both long-term research and timely policy analysis while building the technical and analytical skills needed for a successful career in economics.

This is a two-year opportunity designed for recent graduates who want to deepen their research capabilities, explore the field of economics, and prepare for the next stage of their careers. 

 What You’ll Do 
 Research Assistants work closely with economists and research staff across a range of economic and policy areas, including macroeconomics, microeconomics, finance, and regional economics.
 Responsibilities include:
 Collecting, cleaning, managing, and analyzing economic and financial data.
 Conducting statistical and econometric analysis and developing research code using tools such as Stata, R, Python, and MATLAB.
 Conducting literature reviews and synthesizing academic and policy research.
 Preparing charts, tables, written analysis, presentations, and briefing materials.
 Supporting research papers, publications, and time-sensitive policy analysis.
 Collaborating with economists, researchers, and other Research Assistants across projects.

 Your Development 
 The Research Assistant Program provides opportunities to develop your research, technical, and professional skills through:
 Training in programming, econometrics, data analysis, and research tools.
 Research seminars featuring Chicago Fed economists and visiting scholars.
 Workshops, conferences, coursework, and other learning opportunities.
 Mentorship and professional development focused on graduate study and career planning.
 Building relationships across the Federal Reserve and broader research community.
 The Research Assistant Program is designed to be an important step in your career. RAs pursue futures in either graduate studies of economics, public policy, finance, law, and data science or continue with careers across government, academia, and industry.

 Who We’re Looking For 
 We seek candidates with:
 A bachelor’s degree or higher in economics, finance, statistics, mathematics, computer science, data science, public policy, or a related field with strong economics and mathematical coursework.
 Strong quantitative, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
 Familiarity with statistical programming languages such as Stata, R, Python, or MATLAB.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills.
 The ability to work independently and collaboratively.
 Curiosity, initiative, and a demonstrated interest in economics, research, or public policy.
 Previous research experience is valued but not required. We welcome candidates with a range of academic and professional experiences who demonstrate the skills and intellectual curiosity needed to succeed.

 What We Offer 
 Full-time, two-year position with competitive salary and benefits.
 Direct collaboration with economists and research staff.
 Structured training, mentorship, and professional development.
 Opportunities to participate in coursework, workshops, conferences, and seminars.
 Opportunities to contribute to Chicago Fed research and publications, including potential opportunities for joint authorship.
 A collaborative and supportive Research Assistant community.

 HOW TO APPLY 
 Please submit:
 1-Resume 
 2-Cover letter 
 3 - Undergraduate transcript(s) — unofficial transcripts are acceptable 
 4-Two references with name and contact information 
 5-At least one letter of recommendation - Submitted directly to ResearchAssistantLOR@chi.frb.org by your recommender with your LAST NAME, FIRST NAME in the subject line

 IMPORTANT NOTE:   
 When asked to upload your resume in the Workday Portal, you must upload all supplementary application documents. There will not be an additional prompt to upload documents 2, 3, & 4. You must upload all documents on the same page as your resume. Failure to do so will result in postponing the review of your application.

 Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

 For questions, contact RA.Recruiting@chi.frb.org .

 Learn more about the Chicago Fed Research Assistant Program: 
  https://www.chicagofed.org/research/research-assistant 

 Additional Details  
 The expected starting salary for this position is $75,000 annually in addition to annual performance-based discretionary bonuses. Final salary and offer will be determined based on the applicant’s relevant experience, skills, internal equity, and alignment with geographic and other market data.    
 The Chicago Fed offers benefits to support overall health and financial security. Learn more about our benefits here: https://www.chicagofed.org/careers/thebenefits  
 A continuous learning environment with opportunities to gain new skills and grow your career. 

 Additional Requirements 
 This position requires access to confidential FOMC and or/supervisory information, which is limited to "Protected Individuals" as defined in the U.S. federal immigration law. Protected Individuals include, but are not limited to, U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, and U.S. permanent residents who either are not yet eligible to apply for naturalization or who have applied for naturalization within the requisite timeframe. Individuals who need immigration sponsorship now or in the future are not eligible for this position, including students in F-1 (CPT/OPT/STEM OPT) or J-1 status.

2c3bb6037ae6ca9c.description:
Company 
Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago 

The Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago is recognized as one of the most influential, trusted and prestigious financial institutions in the world. We serve the Seventh District encompassing Iowa and most of Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, and Wisconsin, and is one of the 12 regional Reserve Banks in the United States. Together with the Board of Governors in Washington, D.C., the 12 Banks constitute the nation’s central bank. 

 JOB DESCRIPTION: 
 The Economic Research Internship offers a number of summer research opportunities across each of our departmental teams, inclusive of – but not limited to:  
 Macroeconomics
 Microeconomics
 Financial Economics
 Community Development
 Regional Research

 This program provides students with the opportunity to gain valuable research experience, network with peers in the field, and to work side-by-side with our economists and research assistants to support research and policy work. The program is designed to help students further develop quantitative analysis, critical thinking, and writing skills throughout the summer.

 Summer projects typically ask interns to:
 Support economists in their basic and applied research – inclusive of collecting data, conducting moderately complex statistical analysis, and organizing the presentation of results
 Assist economists with their research and analysis of policy issues and events
 Prepare a variety of charts, tables, and descriptive text for staff economists and department management.

 INTERNSHIP PROGRAM DETAILS: 
 The Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Summer Intern Program is a paid internship that is open to undergraduate, graduate and PHD students.  It begins in June and continues for 12 consecutive weeks. Interns work 40 hours per week and are assigned to one department. 

 These internships are ideal for students looking to build their research portfolios, who have a potential interest in graduate school, or who are considering applying for the Chicago Fed’s Research Assistant program after graduation. Economic Research Interns are given priority consideration for 2028 RA openings providing positive recommendations regarding performance throughout their internship experience. 

 CANDIDATE REQUIREMENTS: 
 Currently pursuing at least a Bachelor’s degree, graduating Fall 2027 or later, in economics, finance, or related field (e.g. statistics, computer science, mathematics, etc.)
 Show evidence of aptitude of quantitative and analytical skills through research experience (curricular/extracurricular)
 Some exposure and experience using data/programming languages (e.g. Stata, R, Python, MATLAB, ArcGIS, etc.)

 ALL APPLICATIONS MUST INCLUDE: 
 1.) A COVER LETTER 
 2.) RESUME 
 3.) UNOFFICIAL TRANSCRIPT(S) 
 4.) Contact information for at least two references (that, if contacted, can speak to your aptitude for research) - please do not submit letters of recommendation.) 

 OTHER THINGS TO KNOW: 
 Salary Range: The anticipated hourly compensation range for this internship is $20 to $33, with the specific rate offered determined by the candidate's academic level.

 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 
 Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship now or in the future.  
 This position may require additional screening requirements due to the information accessed while performing the job. These additional screenings would be initiated at the time of offer acceptance. The screening covers areas such as education/employment verification, criminal history, credit history, and reaches out to your references and people that know you well.
 As a condition of employment, Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago employees must comply with the Bank’s ethics rules, which generally prohibit employees, their spouses/domestic partners, and minor children from owning securities, such as stock, of banks or savings associations or their affiliates, such as bank holding companies and savings and loan holding companies. If you or your spouse/domestic partner or minor child own such securities and would not be willing or able to divest them if you accepted an offer of Bank employment, you should raise this issue with the recruiter for this posting, who can provide you contact information for our ethics official if necessary.

About Northern Trust 

 As a global leader in innovative wealth management, asset servicing, asset management and banking services, Northern Trust (Nasdaq: NTRS) is proud to guide the world’s most successful individuals, families, corporations and institutions. 

 Since 1889, we have aligned our efforts with our three guiding Principles That Endure: Service, Expertise, and Integrity. Together, they reflect the three cornerstones of business conduct which we strive to instill in our employees, whom we call partners, and to provide to our clients and the communities we serve worldwide. 

 With more than 135 years of financial experience and over 24,000 partners, we serve the world’s most sophisticated clients using leading technology and exceptional service. 

 Position Summary: 
 Northern Trust Asset Management is seeking an experienced fixed income trader responsible for the execution of buy and sell orders across client portfolios. The role is primarily focused on taxable and tax-exempt municipal bonds, with opportunities to support electronic trading across other fixed income sectors, including corporate credit and rates products. This role partners closely with Portfolio Managers and fellow traders to ensure efficient execution across a broad range of investment strategies including ETFs, active and index-based funds, institutional accounts, separately managed accounts (SMAs), and wealth management portfolios. 

 Duties and Responsibilities 
 ·       Execute primary and secondary market municipal bond transactions across all sectors in accordance with portfolio manager direction, client objectives, and investment guidelines. 
 ·       Maintain a thorough understanding of the factors influencing bond valuations, including market conditions, supply and demand dynamics, technical factors, relative value considerations, and sector fundamentals. 
 ·       Develop and maintain strong relationships with broker-dealers and trading counterparties to source liquidity, evaluate market opportunities, and achieve best execution. 
 ·         
 ·       Coordinate tax-loss harvesting, account liquidations, invest-ups, cash deployment, and other portfolio-transition activities, including the receipt, execution, and settlement of related trading orders. 
 ·       Collaborate with portfolio managers on portfolio positioning, trading strategy, cash deployment strategies, and implementation decisions consistent with client objectives and prevailing market conditions. 
 ·       Maintain a strong understanding of fixed income investment vehicles, market structure, security characteristics, pricing methodologies, industry trends, and regulatory requirements. 
 ·       Provide portfolio and market analysis to support investment decisions, client communications, and business development efforts for current and prospective clients. 
 ·       Partner with technology, operations, compliance, and external vendors to test, troubleshoot, and improve municipal trading platforms, data flows, reporting, and system integrations. 
 ·       Identify and implement process improvements, automation, controls, and analytical tools that increase trading efficiency, reduce operational risk, and improve scalability. 
 ·       Contribute to electronic trading coverage across other fixed income sectors, including corporate credit, government securities, and rates products, as needed. 

 Competencies / Skills 

 ·       Expertise in electronic fixed income trading, with extensive proficiency across trading platforms including MarketAxess, Tradeweb, and Bloomberg. 
 ·       Preferred experience with OMS and EMS systems such as Aladdin, Perform, and Adroit. 
 ·       Comprehensive knowledge of fixed income markets, investment strategies, portfolio construction, risk management, and credit fundamentals. 
 ·       Strong dealer relationship management skills, with a demonstrated ability to source liquidity, negotiate effectively, and achieve best execution for client portfolios. 
 ·       Excellent communication, analytical, and collaboration skills, with the ability to partner effectively with portfolio managers, traders, research analysts, and operational teams. 

 Experience: 
 ·       Preferred candidates will have a minimum of three-five years municipal bond trading experience. Candidates with investment-grade or corporate bond trading experience will also be considered, provided they have some exposure to or experience in municipal bond trading.

$160,100 - 272,300 USD

Northern Trust provides a comprehensive benefits package including retirement benefits (401k and pension), health and welfare benefits (medical, dental, vision, spending accounts and disability), paid time off, parental and caregiver leave, life & accident insurance, and other voluntary and well-being benefits. Northern Trust also provides a discretionary bonus program that may include an equity component.

3fc054c430ed7391.description:
Excited to grow your career? 

 BBVA is a global company with more than 160 years of history that operates in more than 25 countries where we serve more than 80 million customers. We are more than 121,000 professionals working in multidisciplinary teams with profiles as diverse as financiers, legal experts, data scientists, developers, engineers and designers.

 About the job: 

 Summary of Responsibilities: 
 Help the efforts of the LATAM Loan Syndicate Sales & Trading team (“LSS&T”), which focuses on the underwriting, distribution and trading of syndicated loans in the primary and secondary markets, focused on LATAM Corporate Loans, Project Finance and Infrastructure, and Real Estate. LSS&T works jointly with the teams responsible for the origination, structuring and negotiation of syndicated loans and other credit and portfolio management functions. This role is critical in the continued development of BBVA as an active Lead Arranger and Bookrunner on loan transactions in the LATAM market. 

 LSS&T, in its Syndicate role, is an analytical and advisory function facilitating information flow and decision making regarding the marketability of loans. Loan Syndicate analyzes the loan markets, evaluates financing proposals and recommends terms, conditions, and applicable distribution strategies. 

 For loan underwritings, Loan Syndicate manages loan market risk, generates underwriting proposals, recommends and executes approved de-risking strategies. In each case, Loan Syndicate provides a situation appropriate market risk analysis (the Loan Underwriting Assessment), including supporting data, liquidity analysis, comparable transaction analysis, an analysis of prevailing market conditions, risk mitigation strategies and the appropriate distribution strategy for achieving BBVA’s Sell-Down Target. LSS&T champions the transaction in the underwriting committee and, if sanctioned, presented for final approval also monitors all underwritings and records them in the Open Position Report. 

 In its Sales role, LSS&T acts as primary contact point between BBVA and the loan investor universe, including regional, national and foreign banks and institutional investors (asset and fund managers, insurance companies, pension funds, etc…). Responsibility includes primary distribution of loans when BBVA acts as Lead Arranger and Bookrunner, including for Corporate Loans (IG and Mid Corp), Project Finance and Infrastructure, and Real Estate. In addition, the team works closely with Loan Trading & Portfolio Management on secondary opportunities to source or divest loans for the bank’s portfolios. As well, the team assists relationship managers in sourcing primary and secondary loans that can enhance the Bank’s position with its client base and provide an entry point for prospective clients. 

 The position requires knowledge of the corporate loan market (investment and non-investment grade), the structured aka project finance and infrastructure sectors, real estate and other sectors in which BBVA is active across the Americas. 

 The general responsibilities for the role include but are not limited to the following: 

 Help senior staff to identify underwriting opportunities across the various business lines, working closely with the coverage bankers and origination and structuring teams
 Work with these teams as well as Risk and PM to identify the appropriate level of final hold desired
 Help senior staff to formulate appropriate level of underwriting commitments and associated de-risk strategies to achieve BBVA’s desired final hold
 Help to prepare LUAs to LUC and other business and risk committees as needed
 Maintain working database of investors and ongoing contact with said investors, including with the Sales team
 Help identify investor list for transactions where BBVA is Lead Arranger / Bookrunner and formulate distribution strategy
 Support the organization and management of bank meetings and marketing events, including the preparation of the necessary marketing materials
 During distribution phases of syndications, help research and answer investor questions, prepare syndication trackers and update reports maintain deal pipeline to ensure accurate reporting of all activity and especially open underwriting positions
 Keep track and provide ongoing assessment of pricing trends across sectors and markets
 Prepare loan market commentary & analysis distributed internally on a periodic basis, ie. weekly, monthly, etc..
 Oversee the maintaining of database of loan comparables
 Work with Loan Trading and Portfolio Management on optimizing secondary loan execution for the various portfolio books within BBVA
 Regulatory and compliance obligations including proper documentation of all trades, etc..
 Monitor & support the closing of loan trades by BBVA’s Closing teams as needed
 Provide periodic monitoring and reporting of underwritten positions and sell-down results, and associated economics, to Team Head and Sr. Management.

 Level of Complexity and Risk Involved: 
 Mid-level of complexity. Key component of the Syndicated Finance value chain supporting senior staff.Actively involved in helping to structure, price, and ultimately sell underwritten loans for the Bank. Must have knowledge of multiple loan markets and investor types in Latin America, including Corporate and Mid-Corporate credits, Real Estate and PF and Infrastructure, and understand best practices in the market, including trends in sustainable financing. 

 Skills, knowledge, and abilities/competencies : 
 Degree in Economics, Accounting, Finance or related field. MBA a plus.
 3 to 5 years of experience including roles in either loan syndicate or syndicated finance
 Knowledge of Corporate and Mid-Corporate, Project and Infrastructure finance, and Real Estate Latam loan markets
 Track record of underwriting and successfully syndicating transactions in the LATAM sectors to be covered at similar level of responsibility
